_comment: Which worklog skill modes this MCP server covers, and which it deliberately does not.
test/surface-sync.js checks this file against skills/worklog/modes/registry.md in both
directions, and against the server's live tools/list. A new mode, a removed mode, a
renamed tool or an orphan tool all fail the test.
Every entry is exactly one of `tools` or `exempt`. An exemption names one literal mode
and carries its reason: a pattern or a glob would silently exempt whatever is added later.

`contracts` pins the script and flags each tool passes. surface-sync.js asserts every flag still appears in that script's --help, because a renamed flag is the drift a name check cannot see: the tool keeps working right up to the moment the script rejects it.

help.exempt: The MCP client lists tools itself; a help mode has nothing to wrap.

init.exempt: Session onboarding: preamble, pull, external scan, cache rebuild. It sets up a machine, it does not read or write task memory. memory_status answers the part an agent actually needs when resuming cold.

sync.note: sync is an umbrella that routes by intent: a slug plus flags goes to checkpoint.sh, archive intent goes to archive.sh. Both are now tools, so the routing is the caller's choice rather than a mode. Conversation-WIP detection stays out: it needs judgement and sync itself skips it in non-interactive sessions.

plan.exempt: Three reasoning passes compressed into a markdown block. A pure generator with no vault operation; the model does this work, not a tool. memory_related covers the prior-art probe the mode leans on.

spawn.exempt: Emits a standalone handoff prompt. Pure text generation, no vault operation.

export.exempt: Packages this machine's worklog setup for transfer, with secrets masked. Machine setup, not task memory.

import.exempt: Merges an export artifact into this machine's setup, LLM-judged per file. Machine setup, not task memory.

project.exempt: Multi-task projects: declaration-order sequencing, a depends_on graph and a per-task advisory mutex arbitrated by session id. Deliberately not wrapped yet. The mutex assumes one caller per session, and this server serialises every write through a single in-process queue, so claim/release needs its own design before it is safe to expose.

scrape-slack.exempt: Scrapes Slack for task enrichments behind a mandatory human review gate. An external integration with an approval step, not a memory operation.

review.exempt: Periodic protocol review across structure, skills, commands and performance. A reasoning mode with no fixed vault operation.

extra_tools.memory_search: Slug-grouped search over task bodies and the frontmatter index. No mode of its own; the skill reaches search.sh from inside several modes.
extra_tools.memory_task_create: Creating a task file. The skill does this inside sync and plan rather than as a mode.
extra_tools.memory_related: Prior-art probe over active and archive, and the in-use project slugs. The skill reaches related-search.sh from plan and sync.
